Figure 12: Simulation results over different US climate zones for varying PCM temperatures This analysis sets the limits on the thermal battery size and weight required to meet the thermal loads for 4 hours during peak conditions. Given that the baseline heat pump unit is 5 tons, the thermal battery must provide a thermal load of 240,000 Btu over 4 hours. Given these requirements, the PCM should have a volume of 0.822 m3 and a weight of 1,250 kg. The feasibility analysis is based on the required overall UAs and compactness (m2/m3), which was conducted to evaluate the possibility of using off-the-shelf HXs. Compactness is the ratio of the total PCM surface area to the HX envelope volume. The required overall UA of the thermal battery is between 6000 and 9000 Btu/(h·°F). Initial analysis was carried out using the following assumptions: 1. HX: Serpentine Microchannel 2. Refrigerant heat transfer coefficient: 5000 W/m2K 3. Since the thermal battery / HP unit are on the roof, this may not be feasible for existing buildings. • The R410A refrigerant charge would be at least 5 times higher compared to the original heat pump, due to extra piping required for the thermal battery HXs. Modified System Targets Given the aforementioned practical HP-TES integration challenges, new targets were set based on the highest-selling HP sizes [10] and available TOU hours [76].
